title: RDMBench fixture profile
description: What a *model* is, captured from one unit of it: identity, product category and details, firmware, every DMX personality (name, footprint, E1.37-5 stable ID where the fixture has one), every sensor's definition, and the PIDs it lists — the file format under the library's `profiles/` directory and what `export-profile --out` writes. Harvested self-description: no values, no current state, no slot tables (reading those means switching the fixture's mode).

manufacturer_id.description: ESTA manufacturer ID — the top 16 bits of the brand's UIDs.

model.description: DEVICE_MODEL_DESCRIPTION, when the fixture has one.

model_id.description:
DEVICE_INFO's model ID. Manufacturer-assigned; unique within the
brand, and together with `manufacturer_id` the key of this file.

personalities.description:
Every personality the fixture has, in number order. The current one
is deliberately not recorded: that is the unit's state, not the
model's.

product_category.description: Table A-5 name of the product category, with its code.

product_details.description:
Table A-6 names from PRODUCT_DETAIL_ID_LIST; an unlisted code as
`0xNNNN`.

protocol_version.description: RDM protocol version as `major.minor` (`1.0` for E1.20-2010).

quirks.description:
What this model is known to get **wrong** — see [`Quirk`]. Never
written by [`capture_profile`]: the wire cannot show a fixture
lying, so every entry is a curator's, added from a bench
observation with a method.

sensors.description:
Every sensor's definition, in number order — no values, for the
same reason.

software_version_id.description:
The firmware this was read from. Personalities and sensors can
change between versions — a profile is only ever true of the
firmware that said it.

source.description:
Where this came from: the unit, its firmware, the date. Required by
the sourcing rule, like a PID table's.

supported_parameters.description:
What the fixture listed in SUPPORTED_PARAMETERS (or its enhanced
form), so a reader can tell whether a model has a PID without a
unit in front of them.

HexU16.description: 16-bit value as `0xABCD` (a bare `ABCD` or a plain number is accepted on read).

HexU32.description: 32-bit value as `0xABCD1234` (a bare `ABCD1234` or a plain number is accepted on read).

LoadPlan.description:
The channels of one personality that a load test must hold at a level
of their own rather than at full.

The case that filed it: an ADJ 5PX HEX in its 12-channel personality
with every slot at 255 lights **UV only**, because channel 9 is a
colour macro whose top value overrides the emitters (`docs/bench.md`,
"The load tool meets the 5PX"). A tech reads that out of the manual;
an assistant asked to drive the fixture has no manual, so the profile
carries it. A fact about the model rather than a fault in it, which is
why it is not a [`Quirk`] — and a fact about one personality, since
the same channel number means something else in another.

slots.description:
Each channel, counted from the fixture's start address, and the
level it is held at while the rest of the footprint is at full.

source.description:
Where this came from: the manual and page, and the bench run that
confirmed it. Required, as a quirk's is: a plan that is wrong
drives a fixture into the state the plan exists to avoid.

note.description:
What the channel is and why it is not at full — "Colour macro:
253–255 is UV only". The curator's text, shown verbatim and never
translated.

PersonalityProfile.description:
One DMX personality: name and footprint from DMX_PERSONALITY_DESCRIPTION,
and the stable identifier from E1.37-5's DMX_PERSONALITY_ID where the
fixture has it — the thing a desk profile can be matched against after
a firmware renumbers the list.

load.description:
How to drive this personality for a load test, where full on every
slot is not output — see [`LoadPlan`]. Never written by
[`capture_profile`]: nothing on the wire says which slot is a
colour macro, so every plan is a curator's, from the manual.

Quirk.description:
One thing a model is known to get wrong, and how that was established.

This is the same subject as the rest of the profile — what a model is,
keyed on manufacturer and model ID — so it lives here rather than in a
fourth dataset with its own loader and precedence rules. What a fixture
*is* and what it *lies about* are both facts about the model, and both
are only worth anything with a source attached.

A quirk is never applied to a stored reading: see [`crate::quirks`].

source.description:
How it was established: the bench, the method, the date. Required —
the entry bar for a quirk is a documented observation, because a
quirks table is otherwise where a project's own bugs go to hide.

QuirkKind.description:
The quirks this build knows how to act on.

Deliberately a short list. Each entry has to be something the bench can
*do* something about — a reading it can annotate — not a note about the
model, which is what a manual is for.

anyOf.description:
IDENTIFY_DEVICE (§10.11.1) reads backwards: the unit shows itself
when the flag is `0` and rests when it is `1`. Invisible on the
wire — the flag it reports is the flag it was given — so only a
human watching the fixture can find it, and nothing but an entry
here can tell the bench.

A kind written by a newer build than this one. Carried through
unchanged so a round trip does not drop it, and acted on by
nothing: a bench that cannot name a quirk must not guess at it.

SensorProfile.description:
One sensor's definition, scaled into its unit (a value in `unit`, not
the raw i16), so a reader compares it with a report directly.

range.description: The limits the sensor can report, and the range it calls normal.

records_lowest_highest.description:
Whether SENSOR_VALUE carries lowest / highest detected, and a
RECORD_SENSORS value.

unit.description: Prefix symbol plus Table A-13 unit symbol — `°C`, `mV`, `%`.
